standard.description: This standard specifies standard methods, scales of sampling, sample-size criteria, and criteria for conformity for sampling fresh, frozen, canned, dried, dry-salted fish, and other fishery products (including fish oils) to ensure representative, aseptic samples are drawn for physical, chemical, and microbiological examinations.

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 11427 : 2001 is a statistical sampling methodology and inspection guideline rather than a direct consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp. However, compliance with its sampling scales, container quantities, and testing timelines is strictly mandated in public sector food supply contracts, state fishery department quality audits, import/export inspections (under the Export Inspection Council and EIA), and municipal food safety certifications (including FSSAI audits) across India to validate fish product quality and resolve contractual disputes. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.
requirements: Cans or packages of the same type of pack containing material of the same variety, same grade, and packed at the same place on the same day shall constitute a lot.

If sampling is done before packing into cartons, the equivalent number of cartons shall be computed based on 24 cans to a carton for packs up to 120 g, and 12 cans to a carton for packs larger than 120 g, after which Table 1 scales are applied.

From the selected packages of dried/salted fish, five (5) composite samples shall be drawn aseptically under sterile conditions using sterile knives, and transferred to sterilized, airtight containers.

Samples must be taken within three weeks of delivery, and all tests must be commenced within one week of sampling. If immediate testing is not possible, samples must be packed in airtight containers and tested within a maximum limit of three months.
